name: puma_node_like
display_name: PUMA node (32 nm, simulated, Ankit 2019), 2208 MVMUs of 128 x 128, 16-bit weights

faithfulness.note: Geometry only. The registered geometry resolves with its claim class. The description states no pricing, so the label of each run names the pricing the run resolves. A run that declares a physics profile or constants is priced under them, and one that declares neither refuses absolute area, energy and latency by name.

stated.quote: Memristor crossbars are circuits capable of performing analog matrix-vector multiplications, overcoming the fundamental energy efficiency limitations of digital logic.
We use 16 bit fixed-point precision that provides very high accuracy in inference applications [20, 95].
We conservatively use 2 bits per device, and realize 16-bit MVM operations by combining 8 crossbars via bit-slicing [95]

stated.reads: We conservatively use 2 bits per device

unstated.note: The source states no bias circuit (a bias add would run on the vector functional unit); the registered geometry's bias row is the description's assumption.

stated.quote: We use 16 bit fixed-point precision that provides very high accuracy in inference applications [20, 95].

unstated.note: A 16-bit MVM combines eight 2-bit crossbars by bit-slicing with bit-serial inputs and ADCs per crossbar, merged by shift-and-add (Section 3.2.1): a per-array converter on partial products, not the toolchain's per-core law on the fused accumulator (W47's per-array ADC, not built); the deployment declares one.

stated.note: Each core's vector functional unit adds two vectors (E) and applies ReLU (L), in 16-bit fixed point; pooling is not an instruction of the table (P not stated).

unstated.note: The MVMUs hold programmed memristor weights; the description declares no run-time writable matrix.
